name: AccelDiff ZEUS step skipping
plain: Forks core solvers with a fixed modular skip pattern: steps whose index mod denominator is in a set trigger a skip of the next call, and the derivative is linearly extrapolated in ODE-derivative space. Real outputs alone stay in the history. It is schedule-based, not error-based.
math:
Skip next if i % denominator ∈ modular and acc_start ≤ i < acc_end, with cons_skip < max_interval. Defaults denominator=3, modular={0,1}, acc_start=10, acc_end=45, max_interval=4.
d̂ = d₋₁ + (d₋₁ − d₋₂); x0̂ = x − σ·d̂. caching_mode reuse_interp reuses the same d̂ on odd consecutive skip counts; interp_all recomputes it. Optional Lagrange on x0 past lagrange_step.

props.stages: 0 on skipped steps for single-eval solvers

audit.note: Formula matches the line, but "linearly extrapolated" holds only for the first skip in a run. A skipped step shifts history and re-appends the latest real d, so prev_d[-2]==prev_d[-1] (jiajianxie__ComfyUI-AccelDiff/sampler/zeus.py:188-199). A second consecutive skip therefore gives d̂ = d₋₁ + 0, plain reuse (zeus.py:168). With defaults {0,1}/3 runs are at most 2 skips long, so every second skip is reuse and interp_all "recomputes" the same stale d. acc_start is also clamped to ≥3 (line 111).
